title: How a mortgage payoff works when selling
description: How a mortgage payoff works when selling: the servicer's dated quote, not last month's balance, is the figure the closing statement should match.
summary: Order a payoff quote through your closing date and match that figure on the settlement statement.
body: This is not legal or financial advice. How a mortgage payoff works when selling is a servicer question with a closing-office answer. Last month's statement shows a principal balance as of that statement. A payoff quote adds interest through a date you name and any fee the servicer puts on the quote. The [CFPB guide to closing](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/close/) is the reading for the meeting. The quote is the reading for the number.

Ask for the quote in writing, good through the day you expect to sign. Look for an expiration. If closing moves past that day, order a new quote. Do not multiply a guessed daily rate by the extra days. The title company or closing attorney usually sends the payoff from the sale proceeds. You still read the line. [Seller settlement statement explained](/tips/read-the-settlement-statement-when-it-arrives) is the habit of reading it when it arrives, not in the lobby.

Type the quote into the [net proceeds calculator](/tools/net-proceeds) with the other costs from [Seller closing costs: what sellers pay](/tips/seller-closing-costs). The wire you keep is what remains. A prepayment term, if your note has one, should already be inside the quote. Ask the servicer to point at it if you are unsure. This page will not tell you that your loan has no penalty.

Keep the quote in the closing folder next to the contract. When the statement arrives, the payoff line should match a quote that has not expired. If it does not, stop and ask which document the closing office used. The guide for this topic walks shortage, the next house, and a reverse mortgage. This note is only the ordinary quote. If two quotes exist, use the one that matches the statement date and ask the closer which file they sent.
steps: Request a written payoff quote through your target closing date.
Read the expiration and any fee on the quote.
Enter that figure, not last month's balance, in the net calculator.
Match the settlement statement to the quote before you sign.
Order a new quote if the closing date slips past the expiration.

title: Selling before the mortgage is paid off
description: Selling before the mortgage is paid off is normal when the sale covers the quote. If it does not, write the shortage before you accept an offer.
summary: You can sell with a balance still on the loan if the closing pays the quote or you bring the difference.
body: This is not legal or financial advice. Selling before the mortgage is paid off does not require the balance to be zero on listing day. It requires the quote to be satisfied at closing. If the price, minus the costs you were quoted, covers the payoff quote, the sale can retire the loan. If it does not, you have a shortage. Write that shortage in dollars before you accept an offer.

A shortage is money you bring, a higher price, lower costs, or a decision not to sell. It is not a problem the title company solves by waiting. Ask what form of funds they accept and by what time. A personal check on the morning of closing is a common way to miss the wire cutoff. Get the instruction in writing.

Do not list a price that cannot clear the quote and hope a bidding rush appears. The pricing guide's bottom line includes the payoff. If the bottom line is impossible, the list price is a wish. [How to price my house to sell](/tips/price-the-property-you-have) still applies: price the house you have, with the debt you have.

If someone suggests a short payoff, a deed to the lender, or forgiven debt, stop and talk to the servicer and a tax advisor before you sign anything. Cancelled debt can have tax consequences. Publication 523 is about gain on a home. It is not a map for a shortage. This note stops at the arithmetic: quote versus net. Bring the shortage in the form the closing office names, and ask for the deadline in writing the week before. A delay in those funds can delay the deed the same day.
steps: Put the live payoff quote next to your net sheet.
If the net is short, write the dollar gap.
Ask the closing office how and when you must deliver shortage funds.
Do not accept an offer that cannot close the gap.
Call the servicer and a tax advisor before any short-payoff agreement.

title: Selling a house to buy another
description: Selling a house to buy another is two closings unless a contract ties them. Tell both offices if the sale wire has to fund the purchase.
summary: Sequence the sale and the purchase in writing, and do not promise the next seller a wire that has not closed.
body: This is not legal or financial advice. Selling a house to buy another is two deals. The sale has a payoff quote, a buyer, and a wire. The purchase has a down payment, a lender, and its own closing. The sale proceeds are not the down payment until they arrive and until the purchase contract says how you will pay. If you need the sale to fund the purchase the same day, say that to both closing offices before you are on the calendar.

Same-day closings fail when a payoff quote is late, a buyer wires late, or a bank cutoff passes. Build a day of slack if the contracts allow it. A contingent offer, a longer closing, or a different funding source belongs in the purchase contract, not in a hopeful sentence. Read the contingency so you know what happens if your sale slips.

A rent-back, if you need to stay after you sell, is also a written term with an end date. Do not plan to occupy the sold house for a week because the next house is not ready. [When do sellers have to move out](/tips/match-the-move-out-date-to-the-contract) is the rule: the contract date is the date. Tell the movers only after both dates are signed.

Price the sale with the cash the purchase requires already written on the bottom line. If the sale net cannot cover the down payment and the moving costs you quoted, you do not have a plan. You have two conversations that have not met. The mortgage guide's payoff section is the sale side. This note is only the handoff between the two houses. If either date moves, tell the movers and the other closing office the same day the change is signed.
steps: Write the cash the purchase needs and the net the sale can produce.
Tell both closing offices if the sale must fund the purchase.
Leave time for the wire. Do not book the purchase earlier than the sale can fund.
Put any rent-back or contingency in the contract.
Book the move only after both dates are signed.

title: Selling a house with a reverse mortgage
description: Selling a house with a reverse mortgage still needs a servicer payoff. The CFPB guide explains these loans. The amount owed goes up over time.
summary: A reverse mortgage is a loan. Get the servicer's payoff before you promise anyone what the sale will leave.
body: This is not legal or financial advice. Selling a house with a reverse mortgage is still a payoff. The [CFPB reverse mortgage guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/reverse-mortgages/) explains that a home equity conversion mortgage, the most common type, is for homeowners who are 62 or older, and that the amount owed goes up over time rather than down. An old statement is the wrong figure. The servicer's current payoff quote is the figure the closing can use.

Do not tell heirs what they will receive until that quote is in the file and the other costs are on a net sheet. The balance grew while interest and fees accrued. A sale is often how the loan gets repaid. Read the note for what happens at a sale, and ask the servicer to confirm the quote in writing through your closing date. The ordinary payoff note on this site is the same habit: expiration date, then the settlement line.

Heirs who want to keep the house instead of selling it are in a different conversation with the servicer. This note is about selling. Authority still matters if the borrower has died. The inherited-house guide is about who may sign the deed. A reverse mortgage does not skip that step, and an estate does not erase the lien by itself.

Put the quote into the net calculator with title fees and any broker pay you agreed to. If the quote is larger than the offers you can get, you need the servicer and a lawyer, not a brighter list price. Read the CFPB page before you list so the vocabulary matches the letter in the drawer. Read the quote's expiration the same way you would on any other loan, and order a new one if the date slips.
steps: Read the CFPB reverse-mortgage guide and your loan papers.
Order a written payoff quote through the closing date.
Put that quote on the net sheet before you set a price.
If the owner has died, confirm who may sign before you list.
Do not promise heirs a remainder from an old statement.
